Brand told jurors he couldn't find anyone to give evidence on his behalf after 'devastating' Dispatches documentary
Earlier, Brand told the court that he had struggled to find anyone to give evidence on his behalf, saying the consequences of the September 2023 investigation by the Sunday Times, Times, and Channel 4 Dispatches were “devastating”.
His barrister, Ian White, asked: “Were you able to persuade a single person with relevant evidence to give to come to give evidence on your behalf?”
Brand said: “I have not.”
Winter asked: “Would they touch you with a barge pole?”
Brand said: “No.”
Brand later told the court he did not consider the Dispatches investigation a documentary, saying: “I call it a TV show.”
Russell Brand has denied all the allegations made against him as he took to the stand to give evidence in his trial at Southwark crown court.
The comedian, 51, told the court that his “entire life has been consumed by these allegations”.
Brand said he struggled to find anyone to give evidence on his behalf, saying the consequences of the September 2023 investigation by the Sunday Times, Times, and Channel 4 Dispatches were “devastating”.
He told jurors that he believed consent was “fundamental, essential, necessary and, indeed, in many ways more important than sex itself”.
During cross-examination, Brand admitted he was “obsessed” with sex in his younger years but denied being unable to function without it.
He denied the accusation that he would pretend to be gay to make women trust him.
Brand told the court he could not remember “prancing around” the hotel room after meeting the woman at the Labour party conference in Bournemouth.
“She was shocked when she came out the lavatory, saying that you were … prancing around,” Karmy-Jones said.
Brand replied: “I don’t remember.”
He said it was possible he “jumped on the bed like an ostrich”.
When accused by the prosecutor of “manipulating” his story to fit around the woman’s evidence, Brand replied: “I’m really doing my best to answer the questions as put to me.”
Karmy-Jones put to Brand that he was “pretending to be gay” to gain the trust of the woman who alleged Brand raped her in a hotel room in Bournemouth in 1999.
The jury were shown a short extract from Brand’s book “My Booky Wook”, published in 2007, in which the defendant wrote a caption next to a young picture of himself.
The caption read: “This is the exact moment when I decided to act gay to attract girls.
“It took 15 years to produce results.”
Karmy-Jones said: “That’s something you would do, wasn’t it? That was something you would do to make girls trust you?”
During cross-examination, Brand told the court that he “said very many foolish things as a young man”.
Responding to the prosecutor’s question about not leaving a situation with a woman without a conquest, Brand told the court that was like a riff of a joke made by American film-maker Woody Allen, who reportedly said the only advice his father gave him was about “F-word” women.
Continuing her cross-examination, Karmy-Jones asked Brand whether he had a “goal” of sleeping with 5,000 women. Brand told the court he did not.
Karmy-Jones continued: “You said that consent was fundamentally necessary and in many ways more important than sex itself, that wasn’t what you thought between 1999 and 2009 was it?”
Brand said: “Consent is absolutely non-negotiable.”
Winter moved on to the final count of sexual assault, involving a woman who said she met Brand while working on a project for Channel 4 in 2009. She alleged he demanded a massage and put his head into her groin area, which Brand denied.
Concluding his questions for Brand, Winter said: “Are you guilty or innocent of these allegations?”
Winter has now turned to count 6, in which a woman alleged Brand anally raped her in 2009 after watching his comedy gig at Hammersmith Apollo.
Brand told the court that he had a “striking” and “memorable” sexual encounter with the woman in a dressing room before the alleged incident. He had saved her number on his phone with the initials “AP”, which he told the court meant “anal play”.
Brand told jurors he was “excited and enthusiastic” about meeting her again.

הקומיקאי ראסל בראנד עלה להעיד בבית המשפט בלונדון במסגרת משפט שבו הוא מואשם בעבירות מין שונות, הכוללות אישומים באונס ובתקיפה מינית. במהלך עדותו הכחיש בראנד את כל ההאשמות המיוחסות לו וטען כי ההשלכות של תחקיר תקשורתי משנת 2023 היו הרסניות עבורו. לדבריו, הוא התקשה מאוד למצוא אדם כלשהו שיהיה מוכן להעיד לטובתו במשפט.

במהלך החקירה הנגדית נשאל בראנד על ידי התביעה לגבי אירועים שונים מעברו, כולל טענות על התנהגות פסולה ומערכות יחסים עם נשים. בראנד הגיב לשאלות הנוקבות בנוגע להסכמה, לאורחות חייו בעבר ולפרטים מתוך ספר שפרסם. הוא הדגיש בפני חבר המושבעים כי בעיניו הסכמה היא תנאי בסיסי והכרחי בכל קשר מיני.

המשפט נמשך כשחבר המושבעים ממשיך לשמוע עדויות וטיעונים משני הצדדים בנוגע לסעיפי האישום השונים. בראנד מצדו עומד על חפותו ודוחה מכל וכל את הטענות שהועלו נגדו מצד המתלוננות באירועים השונים לאורך השנים.
